proposal.reason: The registered text supports the drive definition, its 0.1 cm recording precision, the x_i zero-shift convention, and the far-left-to-right motion in the described procedure. It does not state that γ = 0 is aligned with the midpoint of the two pivots or with rotor 1's pivot. It also does not include the network_C state_event table, so the interpretation of equal event_index drive values and any recorded drive-reversal values are unknown from the registered document.

review.reason: The question only asks about coordinate/record conventions and data-table interpretation, without seeking mechanisms or target conclusions. The proposed facts are neutral measurement definitions/procedures and each is directly supported by O001: the drive definition and 0.1 cm ruler precision, the x_i=0 zero-shift convention at gamma=0, and the far-left-to-right single-rotor procedure. The proposal correctly does not assert that gamma=0 is aligned with the midpoint or rotor-1 pivot, and it correctly notes that no network_C state_event table is present in O001, so the equal-event interpretation and drive-reversal values are not established.

facts.statement: The drive γ is defined as the horizontal displacement of the translating rod in centimeters, measured with 0.1 cm precision using a ruler affixed under the rod.
The mounting position x_i of driving spring i on the driving rod is defined so that x_i = 0 corresponds to no shift when the driving rod is at γ = 0.
In the described single-rotor procedure, the driving rod starts on the far left and is gradually moved to the right.
